body:
Do you think this might belong in the V11.3 Input Validation instead of the business logic section? Perhaps 11.3.5?

 _11.1.3 [MODIFIED, MERGED FROM 11.1.5] Verify that business logic limits and validations are implemented as per the application's documentation, to avoid business logic flaws being exploited such as buying items for a negative amount._

comments.body:
So in v4 we had 11.1.3 and 11.1.5 we had two requirements:

| # | Description | L1 | L2 | L3 | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---:| :---: | :---: |
| **11.1.3** | Verify the application has appropriate limits for specific business actions or transactions which are correctly enforced on a per user basis. | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | 770 |
| **11.1.5** | Verify the application has business logic limits or validation to protect against likely business risks or threats, identified using threat modeling or similar methodologies. | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | 841 |

I think the limits concept does not belong in input validation (the original 11.1.3) but the validation concept (mentioned in 11.1.5) does belong there.

I would therefore suggest:

| # | Description | Level | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **11.1.3** | [MODIFIED] Verify that business logic limits are implemented as per the application's documentation, to avoid business logic flaws being exploited such buying more products than allowed on a particular day. | 1 | |
| **11.1.5** | [DELETED, COVERED BY 11.3.1] | | |
| **11.3.1** | [MODIFIED, MOVED FROM 5.1.3, COVERS 11.1.5] Verify that input which is used to make business or security decisions is validated using positive validation, against an allowed list of values, patterns or ranges to enforce business or functional expectations for that input. For L2, input validation should be implemented globally. | 1 | 20 |

What do we think?

I like the proposed concept, but the requirements themselves need some improvements:
* 11.1.3 - "to avoid business logic flaws being exploited such buying more products than allowed on a particular day." - I'm not sure it is a helpful example
* 11.3.1 - "L2, input validation should be implemented globally." - I think it is not intuitive to understand, that "globally" is required since L2 instead of only security decisions for L1.

I like this direction a lot.

11.1.3: Agreed on the example not being helpful. Can you think of another one more appropriate or just drop the example?
11.3.1: Agree, I like the idea of dropping the "globally" portion and make this requirement just L1 and more straight forward.

One possibility considering everyones suggestions would be:

| # | Description | Level | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **11.1.3** | [MODIFIED] Verify that business logic limits are implemented as per the application's documentation, to avoid business logic flaws being exploited. | 1 | |
| **11.1.5** | [DELETED, COVERED BY 11.3.1] | | |
| **11.3.1** | [MODIFIED, MOVED FROM 5.1.3, COVERS 11.1.5] Verify that input which is used to make business or security decisions is validated using positive validation, against an allowed list of values, patterns or ranges to enforce business or functional expectations for that input. | 1 | 20 |

I especially like deleting the "globally" from 11.3.1.

I am comfortable with the update to 11.1.3.

> 11.3.1 - "L2, input validation should be implemented globally." - I think it is not intuitive to understand, that "globally" is required since L2 instead of only security decisions for L1.

So @elarlang this sentence was added after our big discussion over input validation. I am not sure I understand your point here and I would appreciate a suggested updated wording to try and clarify as I am sure you don't want to just delete it :)

Yes, I know from where it came. Just when I watch it now I think it is not clear and understandable, what it means.

It is not a proposal, but the delivered meaning must be something like this:

> Verify that input (for L1 - which is used to make business or security decisions, from L2 - globally for all input) is validated using positive validation, against an allowed list of values, patterns or ranges to enforce business or functional expectations for that input.

If to move the level scoping at the end:
> Verify that input is validated using positive validation, against an allowed list of values, patterns or ranges to enforce business or functional expectations for that input. For L1 it applies to input which is used to make business or security decisions, from L2 it applies globally for all input.

Reanalyzing it again.
* the point for v4.0.3-5.1.3 (v5.0.be-11.3.1) was only "blacklist vs allowlist" validation, so maybe the merge for v4.0.3-11.1.5 and modification should be done into v4.0.3-5.1.4 (v5.0.be-11.3.2)
* as those are not duplicates and in practice got merged, I would use MERGE tagging instead of COVERS

I really do not think the split level adds anything to 11.3.1 and just makes it more confusing. But I like the concept of globally. Maybe a small change will cover the globally and we still have l1 without the split. 

For your consideration:

11.3.1. [MODIFIED, MOVED FROM 5.1.3, COVERS 11.1.5] **_Verify that all input_** is validated using positive validation, against an allowed list of values, patterns or ranges to enforce business or functional expectations for that input.

> Reanalyzing it again.
> 
> * the point for v4.0.3-5.1.3 (v5.0.be-11.3.1) was only "blacklist vs allowlist" validation, so maybe the merge for v4.0.3-11.1.5 and modification should be done into v4.0.3-5.1.4 (v5.0.be-11.3.2)
> * as those are not duplicates and in practice got merged, I would use MERGE tagging instead of COVERS

I am not trying to ignore your comment, I just don't understand. Can you explain what you mean a little more? I want to understand!

My comment was more towards about modification tags, till Josh gets it, it is ok.

The "split-level" topic is something to discuss with Josh, it was important for him.

> the point for v4.0.3-5.1.3 (v5.0.be-11.3.1) was only "blacklist vs allowlist" validation, so maybe the merge for v4.0.3-11.1.5 and modification should be done into v4.0.3-5.1.4 (v5.0.be-11.3.2)

So v4.0.3-5.1.3 (v5.0.be-11.3.1) talks about allow list but I think the requirement was fundamentally interpreted to be about simple input validation based on range, length and values. v4.0.3-5.1.4 (v5.0.be-11.3.2) is more about structured data for which there are more rigid rules. I therefore think v4.0.3-5.1.3 (v5.0.be-11.3.1) is the better fit.

> as those are not duplicates and in practice got merged, I would use MERGE tagging instead of COVERS

I'm comfortable with that

> I really do not think the split level adds anything to 11.3.1 and just makes it more confusing. But I like the concept of globally. Maybe a small change will cover the globally and we still have l1 without the split.

I think global input validation absolutely everywhere is too much of a heavy lift for our slimmed down L1, hence the split.

> I think global input validation absolutely everywhere is too much of a heavy lift for our slimmed down L1, hence the split.

That means the some level 1 apps will not do any validation for some input which is a pretty trivial DOS vector. All input needs at least a length max.

This is my last comment here, I’ll let this go even though I respectfully disagree. 🙏🏼

## ASVS v4.0.3

| # | Description | L1 | L2 | L3 | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---:| :---: | :---: |
| **1.5.1** | Verify that input and output requirements clearly define how to handle and process data based on type, content, and applicable laws, regulations, and other policy compliance. | | ✓ | ✓ | 1029 |
| **5.1.3** | Verify that all input (HTML form fields, REST requests, URL parameters, HTTP headers, cookies, batch files, RSS feeds, etc) is validated using positive validation (allow lists). | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | 20 |
| **5.1.4** | Verify that structured data is strongly typed and validated against a defined schema including allowed characters, length and pattern (e.g. credit card numbers, e-mail addresses, telephone numbers, or validating that two related fields are reasonable, such as checking that suburb and zip/postcode match). | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | 20 |
| **11.1.3** | Verify the application has appropriate limits for specific business actions or transactions which are correctly enforced on a per user basis. | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | 770 |
| **11.1.5** | Verify the application has business logic limits or validation to protect against likely business risks or threats, identified using threat modeling or similar methodologies. | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | 841 |

## ASVS v5.0.be - as it stands at the moment

| # | Description | Level | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **1.11.4** | [ADDED] Verify that expectations for business logic limits and validations are clearly documented including both per-user and also globally across the application. | 2 | |
| **1.11.5** | [ADDED, SPLIT FROM 1.5.1, LEVEL L2 > L1] Verify that input validation rules define how to check the validity of data items against an expected structure. This could be common data formats such as credit card numbers, e-mail addresses, telephone numbers, or it could be an internal data format. | 1 | 20 |
| **1.11.6** | [ADDED, SPLIT FROM 1.5.1, LEVEL L2 > L1] Verify that input validation rules are documented and define how to ensure the logical and contextual consistency of combined data items, such as checking that suburb and zip code match. | 1 | 20 |
| **11.1.3** | [MODIFIED, MERGED FROM 11.1.5] Verify that business logic limits and validations are implemented as per the application's documentation, to avoid business logic flaws being exploited such as buying items for a negative amount. | 1 | |
| **11.1.5** | [DELETED, MERGED TO 11.1.3] | | |
| **11.3.1** | [MODIFIED, MOVED FROM 5.1.3] Verify that input which is used to make business or security decisions is validated using positive validation, against an allowed list of values, patterns or ranges to enforce business or functional expectations for that input. For L2, input validation should be implemented globally. | 1 | 20 |
| **11.3.2** | [ADDED, SPLIT FROM 5.1.4] Verify that data items with an expected structure, and which are used to make business or security decisions, are validated according to the pre-defined rules. For L2, input validation must be implemented globally. | 1 | 20 |
| **11.3.3** | [ADDED, SPLIT FROM 5.1.4, LEVEL L1 > L2] Verify that the application ensures that combinations of related data items are reasonable according to the pre-defined rules. | 2 | 20 |

## Problems to solve

* v4.0.3-5.1.3, v4.0.3-5.1.4 > v5.0.be-11.3.1, v5.0.be-11.3.2
  * v4.0.3-5.1.3 has clear meaning "allow-list validation only", but v5.0.be version of it (v5.0.be-11.3.1) is basically duplicate of v4.0.3-5.1.4 / v5.0.be-11.3.2.
  * in case we want to keep "allow-list only", then there should be de-duplication done between v5.0.be-11.3.1 and v5.0.be-11.3.2
  * in case we don't want "allow-list only" as a stand-alone separate requirement, current v5.0.be-11.3.1 and v5.0.be-11.3.2 can be merged - **I prefer this solution**
* v4.0.3-11.1.3, v4.0.3-11.1.5 > v5.0.be-11.1.3
  * v4.0.3-11.1.5 got merged to v5.0.be-11.1.5
  * the initial topic here was - shold we move v5.0.be-11.1.3 from business logic section into input validation section - I prefer not, but it requires deduplication from validation
  * v5.0.be-11.1.3 - can have direction as proposed by Jim in https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2614#issuecomment-2664090447, but most likely requires pointing out "per user and per application" as it was originally (after merge v5.0.be-11.1.5 into v5.0.be-11.1.3)
  * If there is agreement on those moves, then the modification tag-nightmare starts...

> in case we don't want "allow-list only" as a stand-alone separate requirement, current v5.0.be-11.3.1 and v5.0.be-11.3.2 can be merged - I prefer this solution. 

Same here. Perhaps: 

| # | Description | Level | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **11.3.1** | [DELETED, MERGED TO 11.3.2]  |  |  |
| **11.3.2** | [ADDED, SPLIT FROM 5.1.4, MERGED FROM 11.3.1] Verify that input used to make business or security decisions is validated using positive validation techniques, including allow-list validation and structured validation (for format, pattern and length). For L2, input validation must be implemented globally. | 1 | 20 |
I think all of the other moves you suggest make sense, @elarlang

Ok so I think I have tried to updated this PR so that it reflects what you wrote here @elarlang : https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2614#issuecomment-2672122388

https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/pull/2626/files

Did I miss anything?
I accepted the PR from this issue perspective. I think 11.3.1 requires further work, I'll come back to this one in the future.
